```{python}
#| output: false
import numpy as np
import polars as pl
import requests
import xgboost as xgb
from pathlib import Path
from plotnine import ggplot, aes, geom_line, geom_point, labs, theme_minimal
from great_tables import GT
from IPython.display import HTML, display
from sportsdataverse.nfl.ep_wp import _load_model

ROOT = Path.cwd()
while not (ROOT / "docs" / "models").is_dir() or not (ROOT / "models").is_dir():
    ROOT = ROOT.parent
CACHE = ROOT / "docs" / "models" / ".cache"
CACHE.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
pbp_path = CACHE / "model_pbp_2025.parquet"
if not pbp_path.exists():
    pbp_path.write_bytes(requests.get(
        "https://github.com/sportsdataverse/sportsdataverse-data/releases/download/nfl_model_pbp/model_pbp_2025.parquet",
        timeout=600).content)
pbp = pl.read_parquet(pbp_path)
bst = _load_model("two_pt_model.ubj")

def gt_show(g):
    display(HTML(g.as_raw_html()))
```

The two-point-conversion model estimates the probability a two-point attempt
**succeeds**, given game context. It powers the **go-for-2 vs. extra-point**
branch of the [nfl4th decision](fourth_down.md): the success probability times
two points is compared against the extra-point EV. It is a Python retrain of
nfl4th's 2-pt model, validated against the converted nflverse artifact.

This document is compiled: the response-curve and season sections score the
bundled booster at render time and compare against the latest published
season's empirical conversion rate.

## Model features

**9 features**; one row per two-point attempt (`yardline_100==2`, 2010–2025).
The binary label is `two_point_conv_result=='success'`. A **monotone constraint**
`(0,0,0,0,0,0,1,0,1)` forces success probability to rise with `posteam_spread`
and `posteam_total`.

| Feature | Type | What it encodes |
|---|---|---|
| `era2` / `era3` / `era4` | one-hot | Rule era (2006–13 / 2014–17 / ≥2018). |
| `outdoors` / `retractable` / `dome` | binary | Stadium-type one-hots. |
| `posteam_spread` | numeric | Possession-team spread (team-strength proxy; **monotone ↑**). |
| `total_line` | numeric | Game total. |
| `posteam_total` | numeric | Possession-team implied total (offense quality; **monotone ↑**). |

## The model

**Algorithm.** XGBoost, `objective=binary:logistic`, **21 rounds**, `eta=0.0576`,
`max_depth=8`, with the monotone constraint above — verbatim from the nfl4th R
recipe. A deliberately shallow fit for a small target.

**Evaluation.** Parity P(success) corr **0.8718** — **below** the 0.99 gate, and
honestly so: the residual is **training-data vintage drift**, not a recipe error.

::: {.callout-note}
## Why parity is capped at ~0.87 (not a bug)
The oracle was trained on the **2020-era nflfastR-data RDS** (726 rows, 21 rounds);
current nflverse PBP has since revised those same plays (spread/total backfills,
a few changed 2-pt results). The recipe — features, params, monotone constraints,
filters — is a **verified faithful match**; the residual is irreducible without
the frozen training snapshot, analogous to the [`wpa` SNR ceiling](parity.md).
:::

## The response curve, render time

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Model success probability vs possession-team spread (era4, outdoors, league-median totals) — monotone by constraint; the model is a context-adjusted base rate."
feats = bst.feature_names
grid = pl.DataFrame({"posteam_spread": np.linspace(-14, 14, 29)}).with_columns(
    pl.lit(0).alias("era2"), pl.lit(0).alias("era3"), pl.lit(1).alias("era4"),
    pl.lit(1).alias("outdoors"), pl.lit(0).alias("retractable"), pl.lit(0).alias("dome"),
    pl.lit(44.5).alias("total_line"),
)
grid = grid.with_columns(((pl.col("total_line") - pl.col("posteam_spread")) / 2).alias("posteam_total"))
X = grid.select(feats).to_numpy().astype(np.float32)
p = bst.predict(xgb.DMatrix(X, feature_names=feats))
grid = grid.with_columns(pl.Series("p_success", p))
(
    ggplot(grid.to_pandas(), aes("posteam_spread", "p_success"))
    + geom_line(color="#2a6f97") + geom_point(color="#2a6f97", alpha=0.6)
    + labs(x="possession-team spread (negative = favorite)", y="P(2-pt success)",
           title="Two-point response curve — bundled booster")
    + theme_minimal()
)
```

```{python}
tp = pbp.filter(pl.col("two_point_conv_result").is_in(["success", "failure"]))
emp = float((tp["two_point_conv_result"] == "success").mean()) if tp.height else float("nan")
gt_show(
    GT(pl.DataFrame({
        "check": ["2025 two-point attempts", "empirical success rate",
                  "model range over the spread grid (min)", "model range (max)"],
        "value": [float(tp.height), emp, float(p.min()), float(p.max())],
    }).to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="Render-time two-point evaluation — 2025",
                subtitle="the model's whole dynamic range is a few points around the base rate — by design for a 1,363-attempt target")
    .fmt_number(columns="value", decimals=4)
)
```

## Limitations

The sample is tiny, so the model is near-constant — treat it as a
slightly-context-adjusted base rate, not a sharp per-play estimate. No
play-call, personnel, or defensive context. The decision it feeds is driven
mostly by the ~48% success level against the empirical XP make rate.

## Provenance

| field | value |
|---|---|

| `training_seasons` | 2010–2025 (1,363 attempts) |
| `hyperparameters` | eta=0.0576, max_depth=8, nrounds=21 |
| `lineage` | nfl4th two-point model |

| `distribution` | bundled in sportsdataverse |

## Avenues for improvement & open issues

- **Sparse-sample ceiling** — a documented soft gate (~0.87 parity) because
  the data vintage is thin; pooling college two-point data is a plausible
  transfer-learning experiment.
- **Known issue:** the soft gate means CI tolerates parity misses here —
  reviewers must not read its PASS as equivalent to the hard-gated models.
